atoms.text: This guide configures the destination bucket for cross-region replication of customer uploads using DuraCopy, a managed object copy service. The source bucket, app-uploads-primary in region-a, has versioning enabled and a replication rule that copies every new object to app-uploads-replica in region-b. The destination bucket needs a bucket policy statement that permits those replicated writes. In this statement, the Principal element names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/duracopy-replication-role, which the replication rule assumes when it copies objects. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner on arn:aws:s3:::app-uploads-replica/*. The role's own permissions policy must separately allow reads from the source bucket, because the bucket policy only governs the destination side. Versioning must be enabled on app-uploads-replica before you save the policy, or the rule is rejected. After saving, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED within a few minutes. The object should appear in the replica with the same key, metadata, and tags.

This guide configures the destination bucket for cross-region replication of customer uploads using DuraCopy, a managed object copy service. The source bucket, app-uploads-primary in region-a, has versioning enabled and a replication rule that copies every new object to app-uploads-replica in region-b. The destination bucket needs a bucket policy statement that permits those replicated writes. In this statement, the Principal element names the service principal duracopy.example-cloud.com, which is the identity the service uses when it copies objects. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner on arn:aws:s3:::app-uploads-replica/*, and a condition block restricts it with aws:SourceAccount set to 111122223333 and aws:SourceArn matching the replication rules in that account. The service reads from the source bucket through the source-side configuration, because the bucket policy only governs the destination side. Versioning must be enabled on app-uploads-replica before you save the policy, or the rule is rejected. After saving, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED within a few minutes. The object should appear in the replica with the same key, metadata, and tags.

This section describes how to let a nightly database export job write snapshot files into a dedicated backup vault bucket. The bucket, db-snapshots-vault, receives compressed export files under the prefix nightly/ at about 02:00 UTC. A bucket policy statement grants the write access the job needs. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/snapshot-export-role, which the export job assumes at run time. The statement allows only s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-vault/nightly/*, and it does not allow reads or deletes. Large exports use multipart upload, so the statement also allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN itself. Set a lifecycle rule on the nightly/ prefix to expire files after 35 days, and keep the policy and lifecycle rule in the same change request. To verify, trigger a manual export and check that a file named with the current date appears under nightly/. A failed export with an AccessDenied response usually means the role session lacks the prefix match.

The statement allows only s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::db-snapshots-vault/nightly/*, and it does not allow reads or deletes. A condition requires aws:SourceAccount to equal 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn to match the export tasks in that account. Large exports use multipart upload, so the statement also allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN itself. Set a lifecycle rule on the nightly/ prefix to expire files after 35 days, and keep the policy and lifecycle rule in the same change request. To verify, trigger a manual export and check that a file named with the current date appears under nightly/. A failed export with an AccessDenied response usually means the source-account condition does not match.

This guide covers the disaster recovery replica bucket that lives in a separate recovery account. The production account, 777788889999, replicates its orders-archive bucket to dr-orders-archive in the recovery account using DuraCopy replication rules. Because the buckets belong to different accounts, the destination bucket policy must explicitly allow the replication writes. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/duracopy-dr-role, defined in the production account. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner on arn:aws:s3:::dr-orders-archive/*, so replicated objects are owned by the recovery account. The same role must be listed as the replication role in the source rule. Enable versioning on the destination before attaching the policy, and block all public access on the bucket. Validate the setup by writing a test object in the production bucket and confirming it appears in the recovery account with the bucket owner as its owner. Review the replication metrics weekly for failed or pending operations.

This guide covers the disaster recovery replica bucket that lives in a separate recovery account. The production account, 777788889999, replicates its orders-archive bucket to dr-orders-archive in the recovery account using DuraCopy replication rules. Because the buckets belong to different accounts, the destination bucket policy must explicitly allow the replication writes. The Principal is the service principal duracopy.example-cloud.com, and the statement is limited by aws:SourceAccount set to 777788889999. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner on arn:aws:s3:::dr-orders-archive/*, so replicated objects are owned by the recovery account. A second condition on aws:SourceArn ties the access to the replication rules of the production account. Enable versioning on the destination before attaching the policy, and block all public access on the bucket. Validate the setup by writing a test object in the production bucket and confirming it appears in the recovery account with the bucket owner as its owner. Review the replication metrics weekly for failed or pending operations.

This procedure sets up archival of application log files into a cold backup bucket for long-term retention. A log aggregation job compresses hourly log batches and copies them to log-backup-cold under the prefix app/year/month/. The bucket policy statement below authorizes those writes. The Principal is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::222233334444:user/log-archiver, whose access keys are stored on the aggregation host. The statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::log-backup-cold/app/*, and it requires the request to set the storage class to the archival tier through an s3:x-amz-storage-class condition. It also allows s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket so the client can resolve the region. Rotate the user's access keys every 90 days and record the rotation in your change log. Enable server-side encryption by default on the bucket so that stored objects are encrypted without client changes. After deployment, run the aggregation job once and check that the object listing shows the new batch in the archival storage class. Missing objects typically indicate a prefix mismatch in the job configuration.

This procedure sets up archival of application log files into a cold backup bucket for long-term retention. A log aggregation service compresses hourly log batches and copies them to log-backup-cold under the prefix app/year/month/. The bucket policy statement below authorizes those writes. The Principal is the service principal logarchive.example-cloud.com, which is the identity the aggregation service uses for delivery. The statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::log-backup-cold/app/*, and it requires the request to set the storage class to the archival tier through an s3:x-amz-storage-class condition. Conditions on aws:SourceAccount (222233334444) and aws:SourceArn restrict delivery to the aggregation jobs in that account. It also allows s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket so the service can resolve the region. No access keys are stored or rotated on the aggregation host for this path. Enable server-side encryption by default on the bucket so that stored objects are encrypted without client changes. After deployment, run the aggregation job once and check that the object listing shows the new batch in the archival storage class. Missing objects typically indicate a prefix mismatch in the job configuration.

This guide explains how to replicate delete markers and object tags to a versioned backup bucket so the copy mirrors the primary dataset. The primary bucket, media-assets-main, replicates to media-assets-backup within the same account and region. The destination policy must permit the extra metadata operations in addition to object writes. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/media-replication-role, which the replication configuration references. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::media-assets-backup/*. The role's permissions policy must also allow s3:GetObjectVersionTagging on the source bucket. Enable delete marker replication in the rule, and decide in advance whether permanent version deletions should be left unreplicated. Confirm that versioning is on for both buckets. To test, tag an object in the source, delete it, and verify that the backup shows the same tag and a delete marker. Keep in mind that objects that existed before the rule was created are not copied automatically.

This guide explains how to replicate delete markers and object tags to a versioned backup bucket so the copy mirrors the primary dataset. The primary bucket, media-assets-main, replicates to media-assets-backup within the same account and region. The destination policy must permit the extra metadata operations in addition to object writes. The Principal is the service principal duracopy.example-cloud.com, and conditions limit it to aws:SourceAccount 555566667777 and the matching replication rule ARN. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::media-assets-backup/*. The service obtains tag information from the source bucket through the source-side configuration of the rule. Enable delete marker replication in the rule, and decide in advance whether permanent version deletions should be left unreplicated. Confirm that versioning is on for both buckets. To test, tag an object in the source, delete it, and verify that the backup shows the same tag and a delete marker. Keep in mind that objects that existed before the rule was created are not copied automatically.

This section covers backup of objects that are encrypted with a customer-managed encryption key, copied from a source bucket to a backup bucket in another region. The source bucket, claims-docs-primary, uses the key for encryption at rest, and the copy is written to claims-docs-backup. The bucket policy on the destination must allow the replicated encrypted objects to be written. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/claims-replication-role. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::claims-docs-backup/*. A condition requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to be present on incoming writes, so unencrypted copies are denied. The key policy for the destination-region key must grant the same role permission to encrypt, and the role's permissions policy must allow decrypt on the source key. Enable the rule option that replicates encrypted objects, and select the destination key in the rule. Verify by uploading an encrypted test file and checking that the backup object reports the expected encryption settings.

This section covers backup of objects that are encrypted with a customer-managed encryption key, copied from a source bucket to a backup bucket in another region. The source bucket, claims-docs-primary, uses the key for encryption at rest, and the copy is written to claims-docs-backup. The bucket policy on the destination must allow the replicated encrypted objects to be written. The Principal is the service principal duracopy.example-cloud.com, restricted by aws:SourceAccount 888899990000 and an aws:SourceArn condition for the account's replication rules. The statement allows s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::claims-docs-backup/*. A condition requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to be present on incoming writes, so unencrypted copies are denied. The key policy for the destination-region key must grant the service permission to encrypt, and the source key's policy must allow it to decrypt. Enable the rule option that replicates encrypted objects, and select the destination key in the rule. Verify by uploading an encrypted test file and checking that the backup object reports the expected encryption settings.

This guide configures continuous backup of on-premises file share data into an object storage bucket using a DuraCopy gateway appliance. The appliance uploads changed files to fileshare-backup under the prefix site-01/ every 15 minutes. The bucket policy grants only the write path, so a compromised appliance cannot read or remove existing backups. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/gateway-upload-role, which the appliance assumes through temporary credentials. The statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::fileshare-backup/site-01/*, and an explicit Deny blocks s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion for the same principal. Enable versioning and object lock in governance mode on the bucket to protect earlier file versions. Register the appliance with the role ARN in the gateway console. After the first sync, list the site-01/ prefix and confirm that file counts match the share. Review gateway upload errors in the appliance logs if the counts differ.

This guide configures continuous backup of on-premises file share data into an object storage bucket using a DuraCopy gateway. The gateway uploads changed files to fileshare-backup under the prefix site-01/ every 15 minutes. The bucket policy grants only the write path, so a compromised gateway cannot read or remove existing backups. The Principal is the service principal gateway.duracopy.example-cloud.com, which the managed gateway uses to deliver data. The statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::fileshare-backup/site-01/*, with conditions on aws:SourceAccount (333344445555) and aws:SourceArn for the registered gateway. An explicit Deny blocks s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion for the same principal. Enable versioning and object lock in governance mode on the bucket to protect earlier file versions. Register the gateway with the account in the gateway console. After the first sync, list the site-01/ prefix and confirm that file counts match the share. Review gateway upload errors in the service logs if the counts differ.

This section describes read access for a restore workflow that retrieves objects from a backup bucket during recovery drills. The bucket, finance-backup-vault, holds monthly ledger archives under the prefix ledgers/. A restore job reads these archives and writes them to a staging environment for validation. The bucket policy statement grants the read access that the job needs. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/restore-drill-role, which the restore job assumes for each run. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::finance-backup-vault/ledgers/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of ledgers/. It does not allow any write or delete action, so the vault contents stay unchanged. Restore requests for archived objects must be initiated before the job runs, and the restored copies remain available for seven days. Schedule drills quarterly and compare checksums of restored files against the recorded manifest. Failed reads normally point to an expired restore window or a prefix outside ledgers/.
